water-buffers.title: Calculation toolkit
rows: One pH unit is a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion activity (concentration approximation in dilute solutions).
At equal conjugate base and weak acid, pH = pKa. Use concentrations after any strong acid/base neutralization.
A useful rule of thumb, not an abrupt cutoff. Higher total concentration increases buffer capacity at the same ratio.
0.070 M lactate / 0.080 M lactic acid; pKa 3.74
3.74 + log10(0.875) = 3.68. Concentration ratio is base/acid, not acid/base.
Average the two pKa values that bracket the electrically neutral species. Do not blindly average all pKa values.

Clotting factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S; warfarin blocks vitamin-K recycling.

ch-29.title: DNA repair: do not mix organisms
rows: Small base lesions, e.g. uracil in DNA
DNA glycosylase removes the base first; AP processing, resynthesis, ligation follow.
Human XP commonly involves XPA-XPG; bacterial UvrABC is not a human gene. XP variant: POLH.
Recognizes the newly synthesized strand; human deficiency underlies Lynch syndrome.
HR uses homologous template; NHEJ directly rejoins ends and may introduce sequence changes.
